History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old woman presents via tele-visit with a few-day history of constant, worsening mid-line lower-abdominal pain and new light vaginal bleeding; pregnancy test and urgent in-person pelvic/abdominal assessment arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant “tummy ache” in lower abdomen (mid-line, below umbilicus).  
• Onset/duration: Began “a few days ago,” progressively worsening.  
• Severity: 8/10 at worst.  
• Course: Pain present continuously; episodes become “very bad.”  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding beginning after normal menses ended ~2 weeks ago.  
  – Occasional nausea (no vomiting).  
  – Week-long constipation last week; bowel habit now normal.  
  – Small amount of vaginal discharge.  
• Pertinent negatives: No fever/chills, no shoulder pain, dyspnea, syncope, dysuria, hematuria, hematochezia, diarrhea, or weight loss.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Last menstrual period: 2–3 weeks ago; described as normal.  
• Sexual activity: Regular; last intercourse 4 days ago; etonogestrel implant in situ x 1 year; last home pregnancy test negative 1 month ago.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• No previous surgeries.  
• No prior pregnancies.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon), dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – allergic reaction details not specified.

Social History:
• Occupation: School teacher.  
• Lives with husband and husband’s family.  
• Tobacco: Denies smoking.  
• Alcohol: Denies alcohol use.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  
• Travel: Abroad >1 year ago.

Family History:
• Not discussed / none recorded.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (remote visit).  
• Abdominal/pelvic examination: Not performed.

Investigations:
• Home urine pregnancy test negative 1 month ago.  
• Plan to repeat urine pregnancy test today.  
• Face-to-face appointment arranged for abdominal and pelvic examination.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Worsening lower-abdominal pain with inter-menstrual bleeding in a reproductive-age female on implant contraception; ectopic pregnancy must be excluded, and other gynecologic and gastrointestinal causes considered.

DDx Integration (key possibilities):
1. Ectopic pregnancy – constant pelvic pain + light bleeding; last pregnancy test 1 month ago; contraception failure possible (high-priority rule-out).  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – bilateral pelvic pain, light bleeding/discharge; sexually active; no fever (partial support).  
3. Ovarian torsion / hemorrhagic cyst – severe constant pain with light bleeding possible; pain not clearly unilateral (partial support).

Issue 1: Possible ectopic pregnancy / early pregnancy complication  
• Arrange same-day urine pregnancy test; patient to call immediately if positive.  
• Urgent face-to-face review for abdominal & pelvic exam, quantitative β-hCG, and pelvic ultrasound if pregnancy test positive or high clinical concern.  
• Safety-net: attend ED sooner for worsening pain, dizziness, vomiting, or heavy bleeding.

Issue 2: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) – differential consideration  
• At in-person visit: pelvic exam with cervical swabs for STI screening.  
• Empiric antibiotics per local guidelines if exam or tests confirm PID.  
• Discuss partner notification and safe-sex counseling if PID confirmed.

Issue 3: Non-gynecologic abdominal pain (e.g., constipation, appendicitis, functional bowel)  
• Review bowel pattern; encourage hydration, fiber.  
• Monitor for fevers, migration of pain, anorexia, or change in bowel habits; escalate if occurs.

General plan items:  
• Analgesia: patient may continue OTC analgesics (e.g., paracetamol/ibuprofen) as needed; advise not to exceed recommended doses.  
• Follow-up: Face-to-face appointment booking via support line; clinician to review results and progress.  
• Red-flag advice reiterated: severe pain, inability to keep fluids down, syncope, heavy bleeding → call emergency services.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: No vitals, full medication list, or detailed allergy reaction recorded – to be obtained at in-person visit.  
• No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Minor audio gaps but key clinical data captured.
